title: Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Vent Blockages
description: When fixtures gurgle or drain slowly, the problem often originates in the venting system rather than the drain line itself. Plumbing vents equalize atmospheric pressure within drainage piping, allowing wastewater to flow smoothly while preserving water traps. A blocked vent stack or faulty air admittance valve prevents air from entering the system, creating negative pressure. This vacuum pulls water out of nearby P-traps, releasing sewer gases and causing audible gurgling sounds. Clearing debris from the vent terminal or replacing a sticking air admittance valve restores proper atmospheric balance, restoring normal flow and protecting indoor air quality.
